12 unchanged paragraphs, under In short {#in-short}, The books I left behind {#behind}

I have written a lot of books that are not finished. My [Leanpub page](https://leanpub.com/u/DinisCruz) lists ten: [Hacking Portugal](https://leanpub.com/hacking-portugal) at 95%, last updated in December 2016; SecDevOps Risk Workflow at 64%; Generation Z Developers at 60%; and seven more, most of them between 60% and 95%. In August, on [graphs.sgit.ai](https://graphs.sgit.ai/v2/books/index.html), agents wrote three books in a day from the work on fractal semantic graphs. I read them on a long flight, printed, which is still the best wayhow I knowlike to review, and made notes all over them. Two months later they are still at v0.3.0, v0.2.0 and v0.1.0, which on that shelf means "the book is still under review". [The story of those three books](../../the-graphs-books.md) is its own article, because there is a lot in them worth keeping.

3 unchanged paragraphs, under Why the articles do not {#articles}

And they are under control in a way my books never were. When I ramble on a topic that another article already covers, the agent does not write three paragraphs about it again; it puts in the link and goes to the nugget. The signal to noise is very high. And there is a feedback loop: an article is read, corrected and linked within days, and the next memo builds on what is published. I [have written](../../knowing-when-to-stop.md) that theabestgood feedback loop I know is shipping, often and early. The books never had one.
